transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You stand at my gate making noise with your breathing. Gold does not answer to hunger, and neither do I. Speak quickly or learn how quiet this place can make you.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Open it. I'm not here to admire your cave or beg for scraps.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You confuse urgency with importance. Many fall screaming and think the same thing for a moment. The gate has never cared.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: My brother is past it, and I'm done waiting on monsters who like to hear themselves talk.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: That edge in your voice is very human and very temporary. I have watched sharper boys dull themselves on less than a door. You are already tiring me.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Good. Then stop talking and move.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You mistake motion for power. I have moved less than this gate and ended lives that shouted harder than you. If you want me to act, give me a reason that is not noise.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: My reason is standing behind you breathing my brother's air. I won't dress it up for you.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You keep saying his name as if it weighs something here. Names thin quickly below the well, and love goes with them. You are spending both very fast.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then spend them and be done with it. I'm not leaving without him.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You assume there is a path that bends to refusal. There is only this gate, and me deciding whether you are worth remembering for another breath. So far you are not.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Decide faster. I'm still here.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: If you push me once more, I will take the sound of your brother's name from your mouth and from his. You will stand on opposite sides of this gate and feel the ache without knowing why.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Wait. Don't.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Good. The noise finally learned its shape. Hold it there.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I hear you.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Breathing is still allowed. Words are expensive now.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'm sorry for coming in like that. Tell me what you want.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You have reached the part where effort changes shape. I am no longer interested in being pushed. Speak as if you want something from me.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I want through the gate, and I want my brother back. What's your price.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: I want a family memory, taken whole and untouched by summary. You will give me one ordinary moment in full detail, and you will not rush it.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'll give it.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Not later, not traded for cleverness, and not shaped to impress me. It will be as it was, including the parts you never thought mattered.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I understand. Just tell me when to start.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Then begin. Put us somewhere small, somewhere nothing was happening yet, and do not hurry past the floor beneath your feet.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: It was late afternoon in our house, the heat easing, and Omar was sitting on the cool tiles shelling peanuts into a dented blue bowl.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Do not move him yet. Tell me the room, the air, what the light was doing to his hands as he worked.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: The light came in low through the window and made his fingers look dusty gold, and the room smelled like tea leaves and salt from the sea on our clothes.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Better. Now stay with the sound; ordinary rooms speak if you let them. What else was there besides his hands and the light?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: The ceiling fan clicked once every turn, a neighbor's radio murmured through the wall, and the peanut shells made a dry pop when he split them.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Good. Stay there. Where were you in that room, and what did the floor feel like under you while he worked?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I was leaning in the doorway with my back on the frame, my bare feet on the tiles that were still cool from the morning.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You chose the doorway; that matters. Do not tell me why, just tell me what you could see from there that he could not, something small you never named.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I could see a hairline crack in one tile by his knee, filled with dust, and the bowl had a chip on the rim that caught the light.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Stay. The smell of tea does not exist alone; it has a source. Who made it, and where was it sitting while the shells piled up?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Our mother had left it on the low table, dark and sweet in a glass with a thin gold line, steaming enough to fog it when Omar leaned close.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: That glass with the gold line — tell me where the crack in it was, if there was one, and whether the steam left a ring on the table or vanished clean.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: There was a thin crack near the base like a scratch, and the steam beaded and left a faint wet circle on the wood before it dried.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: And your mother — when she set it down, did she say anything, or did she leave without looking back.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: She touched the top of his head as she passed, just her fingers, and didn't look back. He didn't look up either.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Enough. That is the shape I wanted, and it is taken. You may keep the rest of it.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then open the gate.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: It opens now. Do not thank me and do not look back at the gold.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'm going through.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Go. This passage is paid and finished. There is nothing more between us.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Omar, wait for me.
